newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - 14 AUGUST.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - 14 AUGUST.

text.p: This summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on +44 (0)171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com
-- WARNING ON BASE RATES DESPITE INFLATION HOPES

In the Bank of England's quarterly Inflation Report it has been reported that interest rates are indicating consistency with the government's 2.5 per cent inflation rate target but that the risks still appear to be more on the upside with the recent trend in unemployment that has given rise to the lowest number of people claiming benefit in the UK for 17 years. Base rates have been increased by a quarter-point in each of the last four months giving a rate of seven per cent.
-- MOVE BY SONY AND PHILIPS THREATENS DIGITAL DISC 'WARS'

Electronics firms Sony and Philips, along with US computer equipment maker Hewlett-Packard, have threatened to start another format war by announcing intentions to develop a different format of DVD-Ram advanced computer discs. The original consortium of 11 firms, including Japanese electronics firms Matsushita, Toshiba and Hitatchi has been disrupted by the move by the 3 rogue companies to develop an alternative CD-Video-like advanced information disc that will be in direct competition with the original.
-- ROYAL BANK WILL PAY UP TO 630M STG FOR MIDSHIRES

Royal Bank of Scotland has agreed to buy the Birmingham Midshires building society for between 605-630 million sterling, depending upon the next 12 months profits, giving its 1.2 million customers' payouts averaging up to 850 sterling. Midshires, which has about 300,000 carpet baggers on its membership list, revealed that it could no longer survive on its own.
-- PARIS MAY TAP UTILITY FOR FUNDS TO REDUCE DEFICIT

The French government is expected to ask the directors of the national electricity utility, Electricit de France, for substantial funds to help reduce the national budget deficit in 1998 to bring it belatedly in line with the 3 per cent of gross domestic product requirements of the Maastricht treaty. The government already cut this years deficit with a FFr37.5 billion one-off payment from France Telecom.
-- BUSINESS BACKING FOR WELSH ASSEMBLEY GROWS

The Institute of Directors and the Confederation of British Industry have both expressed the support of the business community for the devolution of Wales by endorsing the Labour party's plans for a Cardiff assembly. The news gives weight to the governments support of devolution which is due for a referendum on September 18.
-- SIB PLANS TO END LOOPHOLE OVER UNIT TRUSTS

The Securities and Investments Board has proposed that its previous ruling concerning the investment of 10 per cent of a unit trusts' portfolio in relatively high risk securities, such as shares not listed on a recognised stock exchange, should also now be extended to include pre-listed, as well as listed, securities. The move follows fund inflation by fund manager Peter Young, that although permissible under the SIB loophole cost Morgon Grenfell's parent company 220 million sterling in compensation.
-- GOLD HANDCUFFS SCHEME MAY TIE CAMELOT CHIEFS

After the recent debacle between Camalot and the secretary for culture, media and sport, Chris Smith, over 'fat-cat' incentive payments, the National Lottery operator Camelot is nearing completion of a new incentive system for its directors and higher management after several of its senior executives have left. This time, however, Camelot intends to informally agree the payment system with government ministers so as not to spark another row.
-- SBC LIFTED BY INVESTMENT BANKING ARM

Swiss Bank Corporation has announced an 84 per cent leap in first-half net income to SFr1.33bn (550m stg), with the greatest contribution coming from SBC's investment banking arm. SBC acquired the UK merchant bank SG Warburg in 1995, and the investment bank SBC Warburg which was created by the deal contributed net income of SFr691m to the results, a 60 per cent increase.
-- AIRTOURS DISPUTES FINDING BY MMC

Airtours, the UK's second-largest package holiday company, has attacked the provisional finding announced last week by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission that travel groups engage in anti-competitive behaviour. David Crossland, the company's chairman, claimed on Wednesday that there was no collusion in the industry, and said that ownership links between travel agents and tour operators actually created greater competition. The full MMC report on the issue is due in November.
-- NETSCAPE LAUNCHES 'PUSH' SOFTWARE

Netscape Communications has launched its latest Internet browser programme, Netscape Communicator, which includes for the first time the company's much-anticipated Netcaster 'push' software. The new technology will allow Internet users to tune in to more than 700 new information and entertainment 'channels', automatically delivered to PC terminals at pre-determined intervals. The Netscape launch comes a few weeks ahead of the expected introduction of a rival version from software giant Microsoft. For a full range of news monitoring services, phone BMC +44-171-377-1742
